thread:
Incident Bot: ALERT: HIGH_SRV_FAILURE_RATE detected in us-west-1c — SRV lookups to consul for _model-backend._tcp.consul failing >5% over 5m. Paging Luca (oncall).
Luca (oncall): acknowledged, joining. Any alerts from customers?
Jorge (support): Two enterprise customers on Dedicated report model load errors and sporadic 504s. Their pools are pinned to us-west-1c.
Priya: Observability shows a spike in coredns SERVERROR and UDP retransmits from coredns -> consul-agent in 1c. The coredns plugin is getting timeouts when doing SRV queries, then returning NXDOMAIN-like errors to clients.
Marta (netops): Network telemetry: we saw an automated route table update rolled out at ~2425309950 to a subset of racks in 1c (BGP change). There are increased asymmetric paths for UDP to the consul proxies. Packet loss up to 12% observed on the UDP flow.
Kai (platform): That route update was part of a scheduled capacity reorg (ticket #INC-2026) but it shouldn't have affected internal peering. I'm pulling the deployment details now.
Luca (oncall): Immediate mitigation plan: 1) divert new model allocation away from 1c 2) enable DNS caching TTL override on coredns 3) restart consul agents in 1c if they are stuck 4) notify customers and escalate pinned Dedicated pools.
Priya: For quick DNS relief, can we increase the negative cache TTL to avoid flapping? We can set coredns configmap to cache SERVFAIL for 30s to reduce churn.
Kai (platform): I can roll a config change to coredns in the 1c namespace. Command: ```kubectl -n infra-1c apply -f coredns-cache-override.yaml``` The change will be next-gen rollout; expect ~30s to apply.
Marta (netops): I'm opening an emergency ticket with the cloud provider networking team referencing the route table job ID. Asking for rollback on the affected racks.
Jorge (support): Sending customers an incident note: "We're investigating intermittent model load failures in us-west-1c and moving traffic to healthy AZs. We'll follow up with root cause once we stabilize."
Incident Bot: Pager routed to Luca (oncall) and Marta (netops). Severity escalated to P1 for affected Dedicated customers.
Luca (oncall): Applied route diversion: updated smart-router policies to avoid allocating new hosts in us-west-1c, and drained existing non-pinned serving instances. Command: ```redwoodctl cluster set-az-weight model-pools --az=us-west-1c --weight=0 --drain=true```
Kai (platform): coredns cache override applied. Config snippet: ```plugins: \
  cache: \
    negative: 30s```
Priya: After cache change, SRV error-rate dropped from 6.5% -> 2.0% within a minute. But we still see intermittent consul-agent timeouts when coredns upstream queries hit those racks.
Marta (netops): Provider acknowledged the regression and started a rollback of the most recent route-table change. ETA 8-12 minutes to full rollback across affected racks. They reported a known automation bug triggered by a malformed announce.
Luca (oncall): For pinned Dedicated customers, we need a targeted plan instead of global drain. Kai, can we trigger an emergency migration for pinned hosts to replicate over to us-west-1a/1b with minimal downtime?
Kai (platform): Yes — we have a hot-standby allocation policy for reserved pools. I'll trigger a controlled failover: ```redwoodctl dedicated migrate --pool-id=RP-2342 --target-az=us-west-1a --mode=live-swap``` This will stream model state and failover. Executing now for the first impacted pool.
Jorge (support): Notifying affected customers that we're performing a live migration for their reserved pool to avoid further errors. ETA ~7-10m for initial migration.
Priya: I'm seeing the consul members in 1c flapping; some agents report TLS handshake timeouts to the leader. Could be UDP packet loss causing retries to pile up. Might need to restart the consul-daemonset in 1c after rollback.
Marta (netops): Provider reports rollback in progress; packet-loss metrics improving: 12% -> 3% in last 2m.
Luca (oncall): Do not restart consul yet — only after the provider confirms stability. Restarting during asymmetric routing may cause re-election thrash. Keep monitoring.
Incident Bot: New annotation: mitigation actions applied: az-weight-zero, coredns negative cache, dedicated live-migrate started.
Kai (platform): First dedicated pool live-swap completed successfully. Model-serving metrics for that customer normalized within 90s. Moving to next pool.
Jorge (support): Customer A acknowledged the migration and reports recovered model loading. Customer B still sees intermittent failures; their pool is larger — migration in progress.
Priya: Once provider finishes rollback, plan: 1) run graceful restart of consul agents in 1c 2) flush coredns caches 3) run smoke tests for SRV lookups at scale.
Marta (netops): Provider confirms rollback completed at ~2425310280. They validated route announcements and BGP convergence.
Luca (oncall): Ok, proceeding with controlled consul restart and coredns cache flush. Priya, coordinate restarts with stagger to avoid mass rejoin.
Priya: Restarting consul agents (stagger 20s nodes): ```kubectl -n consul-1c rollout restart ds/consul-agent -l role=agent``` Restart in progress.
Kai (platform): Flushing coredns caches by restarting coredns pods to clear stale NEG caches: ```kubectl -n infra-1c rollout restart deployment/coredns```
Priya: Consul nodes rejoined and leader is stable. SRV query success rate is back above 99.5%. 5xx rates for model-serving dropped to baseline.
Jorge (support): All customers on the migrated pools report recovery. For any pinned pools where migration wasn't possible, we have a manual remediation plan and Customer Success is reaching out.
Luca (oncall): Marking mitigated at 2425310360. Handoff to Priya for post-incident analysis and to Marta for cloud provider RCA follow-up.
Priya: Postmortem owners will add action items: 1) gate route-table automation with additional canary for internal peering 2) add an automatic fallback DNS cache TTL toggle for SRV spikes 3) test live-migration runbook for pinned Dedicated pools quarterly 4) improve monitoring to detect asymmetric path issues earlier.
Marta (netops): I'll follow up with provider for a permanent fix and ask for a post-rollback incident report.
Jorge (support): Drafting customer-facing timeline and impacted pool list. Will include note that no customer data was lost and that live migrations restored service continuity.
Incident Bot: Incident marked RESOLVED (mitigated) — duration ~6m. Pager closed.
